description.value: The Old Growth Conservancy is a 54-hectare protected forest at 760 metres elevation on West Vancouver's mountainside, containing western redcedars up to 900 years old that survived a golf course development threat in 1990. The Old Growth Conservancy Society runs free guided tours into the reserve's interior, including off-trail sections not normally open to the public, offering a rare encounter with one of BC's last remnants of ancient temperate rainforest. The society's board includes mountain bikers and hikers, and it collaborates with the North Shore Mountain Biking Association on trail access matters in adjacent areas.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms this is an active society managing a protected 54-hectare old-growth forest reserve in West Vancouver, with free guided tours offered seasonally. No cycling-specific infrastructure (bike parking, washrooms, water) is mentioned anywhere on the site. The conservancy itself has 'no formal access' per the website; touring cyclists would interact with it only via pre-booked guided tours meeting at Cypress Bowl Road Parking Lot #5.
concerns: No physical street address available in OSM or on website — only a P.O. Box (P.O. Box 91053, West Vancouver, BC V7V 3N3); tour meeting point is Parking Lot #5 on Cypress Bowl Road.
No phone number in OSM or on website; contact is email-only (ogcs.wv@gmail.com).
Conservancy has 'no formal access' per website — tours require advance reservation by email; not a walk-in attraction.
OSM community tag says 'North Vancouver' but the conservancy and society are explicitly in West Vancouver per the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate and active conservation attraction with seasonal guided tours, but the conservancy has no formal drop-in public access and no confirmed cycling infrastructure; it may serve touring cyclists as a bookable experience but does not meet the required criteria checklist as a standard attraction stop.
enrichment_extras.notes: Tours are free and reservation-based via email. The tours page notes dogs and children under 10 cannot be accommodated. Sturdy footwear required for OGC tours; terrain includes steep off-trail sections.

wow_evidence: 54-ha protected old-growth with 900-year cedars; free guided tours including off-trail interior — rare encounter, tour-conditional day-shaping.
blurb: Protected old-growth forest with 900-year cedars; free guided tours by the conservancy society.
